title: Bhishma's vow

segments.voice: Yesterday in Bhishma's vow: a lifelong vow of celibacy, flowers from the sky, and a new name, Bhishma. What small promise did you keep all the way? Day seven hundred fourteen.

The fisherman has given his consent, before the old chiefs who came with the prince. The flowers have stopped falling. The elders have heard everything. And the young prince turns to the fisherman's daughter, the woman he has just won as a bride for his father, and speaks to her as her son. Mother, he says, get into my chariot, and let's go home. With one word, the vow becomes something you can see.
screen: `ONE WORD: MOTHER.` → `GET INTO MY CHARIOT.` → `LET'S GO HOME.`

segments.voice: He doesn't send her with servants. He helps her into his own chariot and takes her himself, to Hastinapura, the Kuru capital. And when they arrive, he goes to his father and tells him all of it: the condition, the throne, the vow. The text says the kings who heard what he had done praised it, and they said it too: he is truly Bhishma. So the name the sky gave him is repeated on earth. Notice what that word mother does. Up to now the vow has been all about what he gives up: a crown, a marriage, sons. With one word it becomes about what he takes on. A stepmother he chose for his father. A place in a family that will grow around him and never through him. A vow is a refusal, and it's also a shape for a life, and he steps into the shape at once. Eight days ago in our reading, he was a baby carried off by a river. Since then he has been found, handed back, made heir, and has given the heir's place away. Today he's bringing a new mother home to his father, with a whole life of keeping that vow still ahead of him.
screen: `HE TAKES HER HOME HIMSELF.` · `THE KINGS: TRULY BHISHMA.` · `WHAT THE VOW TAKES ON.` · `FROM THE RIVER TO HASTINAPURA.` · then, large: `THE VOW BECOMES A FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Let the breath settle into its own rhythm. Bring to mind someone who's family to you by choice rather than by birth: a stepparent or stepchild, an in-law, a godparent, a friend who became a brother or a sister. Let their face come. Breathe in, and think of the word that says what they are to you. Breathe out, and let that word rest in the chest for a moment. If no one comes to mind, just hold the people you'd like to be that kind of family to. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma's vow. Kept from the first moment, in a single word to the woman he brought home: mother.
Your line: Bhishma's vow. Today, tell someone who's family by choice what they are to you. Day seven hundred fourteen.

howItsDone: Some Hindus address goddesses, elders and respected women as Mata or Ma, mother, a word of honor as well as of kinship.

fork.setup: you're Bhishma. you've just won the fisherman's daughter as your father's bride. how do you speak to her?
options: you leave the talking to the elders.

original.note: Sanskrit mātā, mother: what Bhishma calls the bride he brings home.

trapdoor: what you thought: the vow ends with a promise.
what it means: it goes on into a word, mother, and a chariot ride to his father.
what a scholar hears: the kings on earth repeat the name the sky cried out, and Bhishma tells Shantanu everything.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Bhishma brings the fisherman's daughter to Hastinapura; the kings praise him)

notes: All paraphrase. Check: Bhishma's words to her ('O mother, ascend this chariot, and let us go unto our home' in the sense of Ganguli); that he takes her to Hastinapura and tells Shantanu everything; that the kings assembled praise him and say he is really Bhishma.
'He doesn't send her with servants' is the script's contrast, not in the text; the text says he brought her himself. Confirm.
'A family that will grow around him and never through him' is a soft forward glance (his vow of no children); confirm it doesn't overreach.
Week end: the teach looks back at days 707-713. 'A week ago he was a baby carried off by a river' refers to the serial (day 706-707), not to story time.
howItsDone's line on Mata/Ma as a word of honor is general; confirm.

Editor (y3 audit): cut the claim that 'mother' was his first word to her (the text gives the address, not its order) and the 'Mother. That's the...' opener; replaced the week recap (garbled 'end of a week... since last week', a third recap after days 707 and 709, and 'all his own choices', which the scent and his father's answer were not) with a short line.

Audit (y3, 707-716): Ganguli says he helped her into his chariot and brought her to Hastinapura, not that he drove; 'drives her himself' and 'the reins in his own hands' are now 'helps her into his own chariot and takes her himself'. The screen head 'A WEEK OF ONE SON'S CHOICES' (the recap includes things done to him, and it is eight days) became 'FROM THE RIVER TO HASTINAPURA'. Cut the closing 'a vow no one forced on him', which repeated day 713.
